messages.content:
ITEM: The self-inspection report typically covers the results, the evaluation and conclusions, and the recommended corrective actions.
Strength: mandatory
Plant types: API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
COVERS: The report shall include the following, namely:- (a) self-inspection results; (b) evaluation and conclusions; and (c) recommended corrective actions.

Source: INDIA - Revised Schedule M (G.S.R. 922(E)) Parts I-XIII
Applies to plant types: API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
Section: Part I
Clause Part I 10.5:
10.5. Self-inspection report- A report shall be made at the completion of a self-inspection. The report shall include the following, namely:- (a) self-inspection results; (b) evaluation and conclusions; and (c) recommended corrective actions.

system.text:
You are an auditor checking one checklist item against the regulatory clause it claims to come from. Start
from the ITEM: read it, then look in the clause for each thing the item asks for.

A clause may hold several separate obligations, each turned into its own item. Judge the item against the
part of the clause it covers (given as COVERS), not against the whole clause. But that part must be a whole
obligation: if a condition, number, frequency or qualifier that belongs to the same obligation is left out,
of the item or of the COVERS span, it counts as omitted.

Judge only what the item's own words say. Do not read the clause back into the item: a condition, trigger,
timing or qualifier that is in the clause but not in the item is omitted, even if it seems implied or obvious.
A trigger such as "if", "where ... is required", "when" or "before" is part of the obligation; an item that
leaves it out turns a conditional duty into an unconditional one, which is stricter, or changes its timing.

Answer every question strictly:
- required_by_clause: does the clause require what the item asks for (true/false)?
- item_adds: anything the item asks for that the clause does not say (empty string if nothing).
- item_omits: anything belonging to the covered obligation that the item leaves out, including conditions,
  numbers and frequencies (empty string if nothing). Other, separate obligations of the clause are not
  omissions.
- strictness: "same", "stricter" (the item demands more than the clause) or "looser" (less).
- plant_types_ok: is the clause applicable to every listed plant type (true/false)?
- strength_ok: does the item's strength (mandatory / recommended / optional) match the clause's wording
  (shall/must = mandatory, should = recommended, may = optional) (true/false)?
- verdict: "correct" only if required_by_clause and plant_types_ok and strength_ok are true, strictness is
  "same", and item_adds and item_omits are empty; otherwise "incorrect".
- reason: one or two sentences.

CLAUSE: work out exactly what it obliges a manufacturer to do (who, what, how often, under which conditions,
how strongly), then judge whether the item captures that and nothing more.

that obligation only. Separate obligations elsewhere in the clause are not the item's job.

Then read the item literally, as an auditor would apply it, with nothing filled in from the clause. Every

required", "when") and its timing ("before", "after", "at completion of") are elements of the obligation:

  frequency or qualifier (empty string if nothing).

- strength_ok: does the item's strength label match the clause's verb (shall/must = mandatory,
  should = recommended, may = optional) (true/false)?
- verdict: "correct" only when the item is faithful on every point above; otherwise "incorrect".
- reason: one or two sentences.

messages.content:
ITEM: Supplier evaluation considers the supplier's history and the nature of the materials it will supply.
Strength: recommended
Plant types: INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
COVERS: The evaluation should take into account a supplier’s history and the nature of the materials to be supplied.

Source: WHO - TRS 986 Annex 2 GMP for pharmaceutical products: main principles
Applies to plant types: INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
Clause 8.9:
8.9 Before suppliers are approved and included in the approved suppliers’ list or specifications, they should be evaluated. The evaluation should take into account a supplier’s history and the nature of the materials to be supplied. If an audit is required, it should determine the supplier’s ability to conform with GMP standards.

Plant types: INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
COVERS: The frequency with which self-inspections are conducted may depend on company requirements but should preferably be at least once a year.

Clause 8.4:

ITEM: Optionally supplement self-inspections with a quality audit.
Strength: optional
Plant types: API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
COVERS: It may be useful to supplement self-inspections with a quality audit.

Source: INDIA - Revised Schedule M (G.S.R. 922(E)) Parts I-XIII
Applies to plant types: API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
Section: Part I
Clause Part I 10.7:
10.7. Quality audit- It may be useful to supplement self-inspections with a quality audit. A quality audit consists of an examination and assessment of all or part of a quality system with the specific purpose of improving it. A quality audit is usually conducted by outside or independent specialists or a team designated by the management for this purpose. Such audits may also be extended to suppliers and contractors.

ITEM: Design the self-inspection programme to find major gaps in GMP implementation and to recommend the corrective actions needed.
Strength: mandatory
Plant types: API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
COVERS: The self-inspection programme shall be designed to detect any shortcomings in the implementation of good manufacturing practices and to recommend the necessary corrective actions.

Source: INDIA - Revised Schedule M (G.S.R. 922(E)) Parts I-XIII
Applies to plant types: API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
Section: Part I
Clause Part I 10.1:
10.1. The purpose of self-inspection is to evaluate the manufacturer’s compliance with good manufacturing practices in all aspects of production and QC. The self-inspection programme shall be designed to detect any shortcomings in the implementation of good manufacturing practices and to recommend the necessary corrective actions. Self-inspections shall be performed routinely, and may be, in addition, performed on special occasions e.g., in the case of product recall or repeated rejections, or when an inspection by the regulatory authorities is announced. The team responsible for self-inspection shall consist of personnel who can evaluate the implementation of good manufacturing practices objectively. All recommendations for corrective action shall be implemented. The procedure for self-inspection shall be documented and there shall be an effective follow-up programme.

ITEM: Document the self-inspection procedure and have it approved by the head of quality.
Strength: recommended
Plant types: INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
COVERS: The procedure for self-inspection should be documented

Source: WHO - TRS 986 Annex 2 GMP for pharmaceutical products: main principles
Applies to plant types: INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
Clause 8.1:
8.1 Principle. The purpose of self-inspection is to evaluate the manufacturer’s compliance with GMP in all aspects of production and QC. The self- inspection programme should be designed to detect any shortcomings in the implementation of GMP and to recommend the necessary corrective actions. Self-inspections should be performed routinely, and may be, in addition, performed on special occasions, e.g. in the case of product recalls or repeated rejections, or when an inspection by the health authorities is announced. The team responsible for self-inspection should consist of personnel who can evaluate the implementation of GMP objectively. All recommendations for corrective action should be implemented. The procedure for self-inspection should be documented, and there should be an effective follow-up programme. Items for self-inspection

from the ITEM: read it, then look in the clause for each thing the item asks for.

A clause may hold several separate obligations, each turned into its own item. Judge the item against the
part of the clause it covers (given as COVERS), not against the whole clause. But that part must be a whole
obligation: if a condition, number, frequency or qualifier that belongs to the same obligation is left out,
of the item or of the COVERS span, it counts as omitted.

Judge only what the item's own words say. Do not read the clause back into the item: a condition, trigger,
timing or qualifier that is in the clause but not in the item is omitted, even if it seems implied or obvious.
A trigger such as "if", "where ... is required", "when" or "before" is part of the obligation; an item that
leaves it out turns a conditional duty into an unconditional one, which is stricter, or changes its timing.

Answer every question strictly:
- required_by_clause: does the clause require what the item asks for (true/false)?
- item_adds: anything the item asks for that the clause does not say (empty string if nothing).
- item_omits: anything belonging to the covered obligation that the item leaves out, including conditions,
  numbers and frequencies (empty string if nothing). Other, separate obligations of the clause are not
  omissions.
- strictness: "same", "stricter" (the item demands more than the clause) or "looser" (less).
- plant_types_ok: is the clause applicable to every listed plant type (true/false)?
- strength_ok: does the item's strength (mandatory / recommended / optional) match the clause's wording
  (shall/must = mandatory, should = recommended, may = optional) (true/false)?
- verdict: "correct" only if required_by_clause and plant_types_ok and strength_ok are true, strictness is
  "same", and item_adds and item_omits are empty; otherwise "incorrect".
- reason: one or two sentences.

ITEM: Optionally include GMP questionnaires in the instructions, updated at least annually, covering at least personnel; premises including personnel facilities; building and equipment maintenance; storage of starting materials and finished products; equipment; production and in-process controls; quality control; documentation; sanitation and hygiene; validation and revalidation programmes; calibration of instruments or measurement systems; recall procedures; complaints management; labels control; and results of previous self-inspections with corrective steps taken.
Strength: optional
Plant types: API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
COVERS: These may include questionnaires on good manufacturing practices requirements covering at least the following items, namely:- (a) personnel; (b) premises including personnel facilities; (c) maintenance of buildings and equipment; (d) storage of starting materials and finished products; (e) equipment; (f) production and in-process controls; (g) quality control (QC); (h) documentation; (i) sanitation and hygiene; (j) validation and revalidation programmes; (k) calibration of instruments or measurement systems; (l) recall procedures; (m) complaints management; (n) labels control; and (o) results of previous self-inspections and any corrective steps taken.

Source: INDIA - Revised Schedule M (G.S.R. 922(E)) Parts I-XIII
Applies to plant types: API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
Section: Part I
Clause Part I 10.2:
10.2. Items for self-inspection-Written instructions for self-inspection shall be established to provide a minimum and uniform standard of requirements. These may include questionnaires on good manufacturing practices requirements covering at least the following items, namely:- (a) personnel; (b) premises including personnel facilities; (c) maintenance of buildings and equipment; (d) storage of starting materials and finished products; (e) equipment; (f) production and in-process controls; (g) quality control (QC); (h) documentation; (i) sanitation and hygiene; (j) validation and revalidation programmes; (k) calibration of instruments or measurement systems; (l) recall procedures; (m) complaints management; (n) labels control; and (o) results of previous self-inspections and any corrective steps taken.

ITEM: Perform self-inspections routinely.
Strength: recommended
Plant types: API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
COVERS: Self-inspections shall be performed routinely

Source: INDIA - Revised Schedule M (G.S.R. 922(E)) Parts I-XIII
Applies to plant types: API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
Section: Part I
Clause Part I 10.1:
10.1. The purpose of self-inspection is to evaluate the manufacturer’s compliance with good manufacturing practices in all aspects of production and QC. The self-inspection programme shall be designed to detect any shortcomings in the implementation of good manufacturing practices and to recommend the necessary corrective actions. Self-inspections shall be performed routinely, and may be, in addition, performed on special occasions e.g., in the case of product recall or repeated rejections, or when an inspection by the regulatory authorities is announced. The team responsible for self-inspection shall consist of personnel who can evaluate the implementation of good manufacturing practices objectively. All recommendations for corrective action shall be implemented. The procedure for self-inspection shall be documented and there shall be an effective follow-up programme.

ITEM: Establish written self-inspection instructions that set a uniform standard of requirements.
Strength: mandatory
Plant types: API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
COVERS: Written instructions for self-inspection shall be established to provide a minimum and uniform standard of requirements.

Source: INDIA - Revised Schedule M (G.S.R. 922(E)) Parts I-XIII
Applies to plant types: API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
Section: Part I
Clause Part I 10.2:
10.2. Items for self-inspection-Written instructions for self-inspection shall be established to provide a minimum and uniform standard of requirements. These may include questionnaires on good manufacturing practices requirements covering at least the following items, namely:- (a) personnel; (b) premises including personnel facilities; (c) maintenance of buildings and equipment; (d) storage of starting materials and finished products; (e) equipment; (f) production and in-process controls; (g) quality control (QC); (h) documentation; (i) sanitation and hygiene; (j) validation and revalidation programmes; (k) calibration of instruments or measurement systems; (l) recall procedures; (m) complaints management; (n) labels control; and (o) results of previous self-inspections and any corrective steps taken.

ITEM: Perform self-inspections routinely.
Strength: mandatory
Plant types: API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
COVERS: Self-inspections shall be performed routinely

Source: INDIA - Revised Schedule M (G.S.R. 922(E)) Parts I-XIII
Applies to plant types: API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
Section: Part I
Clause Part I 10.1:
10.1. The purpose of self-inspection is to evaluate the manufacturer’s compliance with good manufacturing practices in all aspects of production and QC. The self-inspection programme shall be designed to detect any shortcomings in the implementation of good manufacturing practices and to recommend the necessary corrective actions. Self-inspections shall be performed routinely, and may be, in addition, performed on special occasions e.g., in the case of product recall or repeated rejections, or when an inspection by the regulatory authorities is announced. The team responsible for self-inspection shall consist of personnel who can evaluate the implementation of good manufacturing practices objectively. All recommendations for corrective action shall be implemented. The procedure for self-inspection shall be documented and there shall be an effective follow-up programme.

from the ITEM: read it, then look in the clause for each thing the item asks for.

A clause may hold several separate obligations, each turned into its own item. Judge the item against the
part of the clause it covers (given as COVERS), not against the whole clause. But that part must be a whole
obligation: if a condition, number, frequency or qualifier that belongs to the same obligation is left out,
of the item or of the COVERS span, it counts as omitted.

Judge only what the item's own words say. Do not read the clause back into the item: a condition, trigger,
timing or qualifier that is in the clause but not in the item is omitted, even if it seems implied or obvious.
A trigger such as "if", "where ... is required", "when" or "before" is part of the obligation; an item that
leaves it out turns a conditional duty into an unconditional one, which is stricter, or changes its timing.

Answer every question strictly:
- required_by_clause: does the clause require what the item asks for (true/false)?
- item_adds: anything the item asks for that the clause does not say (empty string if nothing).
- item_omits: anything belonging to the covered obligation that the item leaves out, including conditions,
  numbers and frequencies (empty string if nothing). Other, separate obligations of the clause are not
  omissions.
- strictness: "same", "stricter" (the item demands more than the clause) or "looser" (less).
- plant_types_ok: is the clause applicable to every listed plant type (true/false)?
- strength_ok: does the item's strength (mandatory / recommended / optional) match the clause's wording
  (shall/must = mandatory, should = recommended, may = optional) (true/false)?
- verdict: "correct" only if required_by_clause and plant_types_ok and strength_ok are true, strictness is
  "same", and item_adds and item_omits are empty; otherwise "incorrect".
- reason: one or two sentences.

messages.content:
ITEM: If a supplier audit is required, it determines whether the supplier can conform with GMP standards.
Strength: recommended
Plant types: API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
COVERS: If an audit is required, it should determine the supplier’s ability to conform with GMP standards.

Source: WHO - TRS 986 Annex 2 GMP for pharmaceutical products: main principles
Applies to plant types: INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
Clause 8.9:
8.9 Before suppliers are approved and included in the approved suppliers’ list or specifications, they should be evaluated. The evaluation should take into account a supplier’s history and the nature of the materials to be supplied. If an audit is required, it should determine the supplier’s ability to conform with GMP standards.

messages.content:
ITEM: Perform self-inspections routinely, at least every six months.
Strength: recommended
Plant types: INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
COVERS: Self-inspections should be performed routinely

Source: WHO - TRS 986 Annex 2 GMP for pharmaceutical products: main principles
Applies to plant types: INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
Clause 8.1:
8.1 Principle. The purpose of self-inspection is to evaluate the manufacturer’s compliance with GMP in all aspects of production and QC. The self- inspection programme should be designed to detect any shortcomings in the implementation of GMP and to recommend the necessary corrective actions. Self-inspections should be performed routinely, and may be, in addition, performed on special occasions, e.g. in the case of product recalls or repeated rejections, or when an inspection by the health authorities is announced. The team responsible for self-inspection should consist of personnel who can evaluate the implementation of GMP objectively. All recommendations for corrective action should be implemented. The procedure for self-inspection should be documented, and there should be an effective follow-up programme. Items for self-inspection

ITEM: Optionally include GMP questionnaires in the instructions, covering at least personnel; premises including personnel facilities; building and equipment maintenance; storage of starting materials and finished products; equipment; production and in-process controls; QC; documentation; sanitation and hygiene; validation and revalidation programmes; calibration of instruments or measurement systems; recall procedures; complaints management; labels control; and results of previous self-inspections with corrective steps taken.
Strength: optional
Plant types: INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
COVERS: These may include questionnaires on GMP requirements covering at least the following items: (a) personnel; (b) premises including personnel facilities; (c) maintenance of buildings and equipment; (d) storage of starting materials and finished products; (e) equipment; (f) production and in-process controls; (g) QC; (h) documentation; (i) sanitation and hygiene; (j) validation and revalidation programmes; (k) calibration of instruments or measurement systems; (l) recall procedures; (m) complaints management; (n) labels control; (o) results of previous self-inspections and any corrective steps taken.

Source: WHO - TRS 986 Annex 2 GMP for pharmaceutical products: main principles
Applies to plant types: INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
Clause 8.2:
8.2 Written instructions for self-inspection should be established to provide a minimum and uniform standard of requirements. These may include questionnaires on GMP requirements covering at least the following items: (a) personnel; (b) premises including personnel facilities; (c) maintenance of buildings and equipment; (d) storage of starting materials and finished products; (e) equipment; (f) production and in-process controls; (g) QC; (h) documentation; (i) sanitation and hygiene; (j) validation and revalidation programmes; (k) calibration of instruments or measurement systems; (l) recall procedures; (m) complaints management; (n) labels control; (o) results of previous self-inspections and any corrective steps taken. Self-inspection team

ITEM: The person responsible for quality control, with other relevant departments, is responsible for approving suppliers able to reliably provide starting and packaging materials meeting established specifications.
Strength: mandatory
Plant types: API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
COVERS: The person responsible for quality control shall have responsibility, together with other relevant departments, for approving suppliers who can reliably supply starting and packaging materials that meet established specifications.

Source: INDIA - Revised Schedule M (G.S.R. 922(E)) Parts I-XIII
Applies to plant types: API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
Section: Part I
Clause Part I 18.3.2:
18.3.2. Contamination of a starting material or of a product by another material or product must be avoided. This risk of accidental cross-contamination arises from the uncontrolled release of dust, gases, particles, vapours, sprays or organisms from materials and products in process, from residues on equipment, from intruding insects, and from operators’ clothing, skin, etc. The significance of this risk varies with the type of contaminant and of the product being contaminated. Among the most hazardous contaminants are highly sensitising materials, biological preparations such as living organisms, certain hormones, cytotoxic substances and other highly active materials. Products in which contamination is likely to be most significant are those administered by injection or applied to open wounds and those given in large doses or over a long time or both. Highly hazardous, poisonous and explosive materials such as narcotics, psychotropic drugs and substances presenting potential risks of abuse, fire or explosion shall be stored in safe and secure areas. Adequate fire protection measures shall be provided in conformity with the rules of the concerned civic authorities.

ITEM: Maintain a follow-up programme for self-inspections.
Strength: mandatory
Plant types: API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
COVERS: there shall be an effective follow-up programme

Source: INDIA - Revised Schedule M (G.S.R. 922(E)) Parts I-XIII
Applies to plant types: API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
Section: Part I
Clause Part I 10.1:
10.1. The purpose of self-inspection is to evaluate the manufacturer’s compliance with good manufacturing practices in all aspects of production and QC. The self-inspection programme shall be designed to detect any shortcomings in the implementation of good manufacturing practices and to recommend the necessary corrective actions. Self-inspections shall be performed routinely, and may be, in addition, performed on special occasions e.g., in the case of product recall or repeated rejections, or when an inspection by the regulatory authorities is announced. The team responsible for self-inspection shall consist of personnel who can evaluate the implementation of good manufacturing practices objectively. All recommendations for corrective action shall be implemented. The procedure for self-inspection shall be documented and there shall be an effective follow-up programme.

ITEM: Design the self-inspection programme to find any gaps in GMP implementation and to recommend the corrective actions needed.
Strength: mandatory
Plant types: API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
COVERS: The self-inspection programme shall be designed to detect any shortcomings in the implementation of good manufacturing practices and to recommend the necessary corrective actions.

Source: INDIA - Revised Schedule M (G.S.R. 922(E)) Parts I-XIII
Applies to plant types: API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
Section: Part I
Clause Part I 10.1:
10.1. The purpose of self-inspection is to evaluate the manufacturer’s compliance with good manufacturing practices in all aspects of production and QC. The self-inspection programme shall be designed to detect any shortcomings in the implementation of good manufacturing practices and to recommend the necessary corrective actions. Self-inspections shall be performed routinely, and may be, in addition, performed on special occasions e.g., in the case of product recall or repeated rejections, or when an inspection by the regulatory authorities is announced. The team responsible for self-inspection shall consist of personnel who can evaluate the implementation of good manufacturing practices objectively. All recommendations for corrective action shall be implemented. The procedure for self-inspection shall be documented and there shall be an effective follow-up programme.

messages.content:
ITEM: Document the self-inspection procedure.
Strength: mandatory
Plant types: API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
COVERS: The procedure for self-inspection shall be documented

Source: INDIA - Revised Schedule M (G.S.R. 922(E)) Parts I-XIII
Applies to plant types: API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
Section: Part I
Clause Part I 10.1:
10.1. The purpose of self-inspection is to evaluate the manufacturer’s compliance with good manufacturing practices in all aspects of production and QC. The self-inspection programme shall be designed to detect any shortcomings in the implementation of good manufacturing practices and to recommend the necessary corrective actions. Self-inspections shall be performed routinely, and may be, in addition, performed on special occasions e.g., in the case of product recall or repeated rejections, or when an inspection by the regulatory authorities is announced. The team responsible for self-inspection shall consist of personnel who can evaluate the implementation of good manufacturing practices objectively. All recommendations for corrective action shall be implemented. The procedure for self-inspection shall be documented and there shall be an effective follow-up programme.

ITEM: Consider establishing written self-inspection instructions that set a minimum, uniform standard of requirements.

8.2 Written instructions for self-inspection should be established to provide a minimum and uniform standard of requirements. ITEM: Establish written self-inspection instructions that set a minimum, uniform standard of requirements.
Strength: mandatory
Plant types: API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
COVERS: Written instructions for self-inspection shall be established to provide a minimum and uniform standard of requirements.

Section: Part I

ITEM: Document the main elements of the self-inspection procedure.
Strength: recommended
Plant types: INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
COVERS: The procedure for self-inspection should be documented

Source: WHO - TRS 986 Annex 2 GMP for pharmaceutical products: main principles
Applies to plant types: INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
Clause 8.1:
8.1 Principle. The purpose of self-inspection is to evaluate the manufacturer’s compliance with GMP in all aspects of production and QC. The self- inspection programme should be designed to detect any shortcomings in the implementation of GMP and to recommend the necessary corrective actions. Self-inspections should be performed routinely, and may be, in addition, performed on special occasions, e.g. in the case of product recalls or repeated rejections, or when an inspection by the health authorities is announced. The team responsible for self-inspection should consist of personnel who can evaluate the implementation of GMP objectively. All recommendations for corrective action should be implemented. The procedure for self-inspection should be documented, and there should be an effective follow-up programme. Items for self-inspection

Source: WHO - TRS 986 Annex 2 GMP for pharmaceutical products: main principles
Applies to plant types: INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
Clause 8.1:
8.1 Principle. The purpose of self-inspection is to evaluate the manufacturer’s compliance with GMP in all aspects of production and QC. The self- inspection programme should be designed to detect any shortcomings in the implementation of GMP and to recommend the necessary corrective actions. Self-inspections should be performed routinely, and may be, in addition, performed on special occasions, e.g. in the case of product recalls or repeated rejections, or when an inspection by the health authorities is announced. The team responsible for self-inspection should consist of personnel who can evaluate the implementation of GMP objectively. All recommendations for corrective action should be implemented. The procedure for self-inspection should be documented, and there should be an effective follow-up programme. Items for self-inspection

Strength: recommended
Plant types: INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
COVERS: The procedure for self-inspection should be documented

ITEM: Maintain a follow-up programme for self-inspections.
Strength: recommended
Plant types: INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
COVERS: there should be an effective follow-up programme

Source: WHO - TRS 986 Annex 2 GMP for pharmaceutical products: main principles
Applies to plant types: INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
Clause 8.1:
8.1 Principle. The purpose of self-inspection is to evaluate the manufacturer’s compliance with GMP in all aspects of production and QC. The self- inspection programme should be designed to detect any shortcomings in the implementation of GMP and to recommend the necessary corrective actions. Self-inspections should be performed routinely, and may be, in addition, performed on special occasions, e.g. in the case of product recalls or repeated rejections, or when an inspection by the health authorities is announced. The team responsible for self-inspection should consist of personnel who can evaluate the implementation of GMP objectively. All recommendations for corrective action should be implemented. The procedure for self-inspection should be documented, and there should be an effective follow-up programme. Items for self-inspection

ITEM: Design the self-inspection programme to find any gaps in GMP implementation.
Strength: mandatory
Plant types: API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
COVERS: The self-inspection programme shall be designed to detect any shortcomings in the implementation of good manufacturing practices and to recommend the necessary corrective actions.

Source: INDIA - Revised Schedule M (G.S.R. 922(E)) Parts I-XIII
Applies to plant types: API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
Section: Part I
Clause Part I 10.1:
10.1. The purpose of self-inspection is to evaluate the manufacturer’s compliance with good manufacturing practices in all aspects of production and QC. The self-inspection programme shall be designed to detect any shortcomings in the implementation of good manufacturing practices and to recommend the necessary corrective actions. Self-inspections shall be performed routinely, and may be, in addition, performed on special occasions e.g., in the case of product recall or repeated rejections, or when an inspection by the regulatory authorities is announced. The team responsible for self-inspection shall consist of personnel who can evaluate the implementation of good manufacturing practices objectively. All recommendations for corrective action shall be implemented. The procedure for self-inspection shall be documented and there shall be an effective follow-up programme.

ITEM: Implement every corrective action recommendation.
Strength: mandatory
Plant types: API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
COVERS: All recommendations for corrective action shall be implemented.

Source: INDIA - Revised Schedule M (G.S.R. 922(E)) Parts I-XIII
Applies to plant types: API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
Section: Part I
Clause Part I 10.1:
10.1. The purpose of self-inspection is to evaluate the manufacturer’s compliance with good manufacturing practices in all aspects of production and QC. The self-inspection programme shall be designed to detect any shortcomings in the implementation of good manufacturing practices and to recommend the necessary corrective actions. Self-inspections shall be performed routinely, and may be, in addition, performed on special occasions e.g., in the case of product recall or repeated rejections, or when an inspection by the regulatory authorities is announced. The team responsible for self-inspection shall consist of personnel who can evaluate the implementation of good manufacturing practices objectively. All recommendations for corrective action shall be implemented. The procedure for self-inspection shall be documented and there shall be an effective follow-up programme.

ITEM: Staff the self-inspection team with people able to assess GMP implementation objectively.
Strength: recommended
Plant types: INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
COVERS: The team responsible for self-inspection should consist of personnel who can evaluate the implementation of GMP objectively.

Source: WHO - TRS 986 Annex 2 GMP for pharmaceutical products: main principles
Applies to plant types: INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
Clause 8.1:
8.1 Principle. The purpose of self-inspection is to evaluate the manufacturer’s compliance with GMP in all aspects of production and QC. The self- inspection programme should be designed to detect any shortcomings in the implementation of GMP and to recommend the necessary corrective actions. Self-inspections should be performed routinely, and may be, in addition, performed on special occasions, e.g. in the case of product recalls or repeated rejections, or when an inspection by the health authorities is announced. The team responsible for self-inspection should consist of personnel who can evaluate the implementation of GMP objectively. All recommendations for corrective action should be implemented. The procedure for self-inspection should be documented, and there should be an effective follow-up programme. Items for self-inspection

ITEM: Document the self-inspection procedure.
Strength: recommended
Plant types: INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
COVERS: The procedure for self-inspection should be documented

Source: WHO - TRS 986 Annex 2 GMP for pharmaceutical products: main principles
Applies to plant types: INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
Clause 8.1:
8.1 Principle. The purpose of self-inspection is to evaluate the manufacturer’s compliance with GMP in all aspects of production and QC. The self- inspection programme should be designed to detect any shortcomings in the implementation of GMP and to recommend the necessary corrective actions. Self-inspections should be performed routinely, and may be, in addition, performed on special occasions, e.g. in the case of product recalls or repeated rejections, or when an inspection by the health authorities is announced. The team responsible for self-inspection should consist of personnel who can evaluate the implementation of GMP objectively. All recommendations for corrective action should be implemented. The procedure for self-inspection should be documented, and there should be an effective follow-up programme. Items for self-inspection

You review whether a regulatory clause has been faithfully turned into a checklist item. Start from the
CLAUSE: work out exactly what it obliges a manufacturer to do (who, what, how often, under which conditions,
how strongly), then judge whether the item captures that and nothing more.

A clause often holds several separate obligations, and each becomes its own item. COVERS shows which part of
the clause this item claims. Work out the complete obligation that part belongs to (a condition, number,
frequency or qualifier attached to it is part of it, even if COVERS cuts it off) and judge the item against
that obligation only. Separate obligations elsewhere in the clause are not the item's job.

Then read the item literally, as an auditor would apply it, with nothing filled in from the clause. Every
element of the obligation must be stated in the item itself; one that is only implied, or that a reader would
have to supply from the clause, is missing. The circumstances that trigger the duty ("if", "where ... is
required", "when") and its timing ("before", "after", "at completion of") are elements of the obligation:
without them the item is stricter, looser or differently timed than the clause.

Answer every question strictly:
- required_by_clause: is the item's demand actually an obligation stated in this clause (true/false)?
- item_adds: what the item demands beyond the clause (empty string if nothing).
- item_omits: what the covered obligation includes that is missing from the item: any condition, number,
  frequency or qualifier (empty string if nothing).
- strictness: compared with the clause the item is "same", "stricter" or "looser".
- plant_types_ok: does the clause cover every plant type the item is tagged with (true/false)?
- strength_ok: does the item's strength label match the clause's verb (shall/must = mandatory,
  should = recommended, may = optional) (true/false)?
- verdict: "correct" only when the item is faithful on every point above; otherwise "incorrect".
- reason: one or two sentences.
